Name: Fishbot
Author: adroslice
Description:
[size=6][b]Fishbot[/b][/size]
This is a Stardew Valley mod that can automate the following tasks in a way that doesn't feel cheaty:[list][*]Casting your fishing rod
[*]Reeling in a fish when it nibbles
[*][b]Emulate a real player in playing the fishing minigame by using a sophisticated strategy, catching fish and treasure[/b]
[*]Stow away your catch
[*]Loot any caught treasure
[*]Eat the best available food when falling below 10 energy with a configurable max sGPE (Sell-Price in G per Energy)
[*]Pause (by opening the menu) when falling below 10 energy if auto-eating is disabled or no good food is available
[*]Pause once per day after a configurable time
[/list]
Any of these can be disabled individually in the configuration (GMCM is supported), much like the handy little [b]Bubble Radar[/b] that'll point you to success.

A configurable hotkey (F5 by default) is used to toggle the enabled automations. You must have your fishing rod equipped for this. The default options should serve most players very well!

[size=5][b]About the Strategy: FishingAutomatonPlus[/b][/size]
I developed this mod because I wanted an auto-fisher for my future min/max journeys that performed well without feeling cheaty. Most of the auto-fisher mods I have looked at basically just skip the minigame and guarantee you a perfect catch and treasure, but that's simply way too overpowered.

I did come across one mod that set out to achieve what I wanted it to: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2527?tab=posts]Fishing Automaton[/url]. Unfortunately, this mod has been broken for quite a while, and it seems unlikely that the Author will pick it back up, but huge credits to Drynwynn. [b]The main strategy implemented now is named FishingAutomatonPlus, because it is a heavily modified version of the strategy used in that mod[/b].

All significant parameters can be modified through the configuration, though the default values should be fairly well-tuned.
If you're struggling to get catches, consider reducing the size of the game window. I've found it performs better at lower resolutions, though the reason why I will still need to investigate.

More information and the MIT-Licensed source code can be found on my [url=https://git.ulra.eu/adro/sdv-fishbot]Forgejo[/url].
